clue.text: Clear person, should he be set free

parts.note: a man is a person
an inverted conditional: 'should he be' means the same as 'if he be'

indicators.note: set free suggests the letters of the word set are loosed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question of whether a prisoner ought to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should he be' is an old-fashioned way of saying 'if he be', giving IF; 'free' rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is obvious and plain to see, which is the adjective sense of clear.

clue.text: Spanish couple embracing in grass

indicators.note: one name of the couple holds the other in its arms, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: Maria is a common Spanish woman's name
Juan is a common Spanish man's name

explanation.surface: Two Spaniards cuddle on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish couple' supplies a typical woman's name and a typical man's name, with 'embracing' signalling that the woman holds the man inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is a slang name for cannabis, the drug also known by this Mexican Spanish word.

clue.text: Nappy-changing dad wraps son, he reports

indicators.note: the father wraps the baby, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a 'new man' is a modern father who shares childcare such as changing nappies

explanation.surface: A modern father swaddles his baby boy.
explanation.walkthrough: A NEW MAN is the British term for a man who takes an equal share of housework and childcare; a nappy is a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who reports the news; the definition is a description of what such a person does.

clue.text: Slow crescendo accompanied a flute part, rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
only part of the words accompanied a flute is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A musical score note: an instrument's line swelling upwards beside the flute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes NIEDAF from accompaNIED A Flute, and 'rising' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual increase in sound volume from silence, the audio equivalent of a film image gradually appearing.

clue.text: Students up on soap about the tanner

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, a British body

indicators.note: the bar of soap goes about, or around, the next word

parts.note: soap comes in a bar

explanation.surface: Students are hooked on a TV soap opera about the tanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the union's initials upside down in this down clue; 'about' signals the containment. A tanner was also an old British sixpence coin, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying in the sun to brown the skin is getting a tan, so is a tanner in a playful sense.

clue.text: Carbon's gradual assimilation is missing in well-organised world

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: the word is is missing, so those letters are removed

parts.note: osmosis is figuratively the gradual absorption of ideas or knowledge

explanation.surface: A science lesson about how carbon is gradually absorbed into an orderly world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes the word is out of the scientific term, leaving OSMOS. Cosmos comes from the Greek for order, hence 'well-organised'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word means order, and is used for the universe seen as an ordered, harmonious system.

clue.text: Cold blow carries in warm one

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: the punch carries, or holds, the next word inside it

parts.note: a hook is a curved punch in boxing

explanation.surface: A cold wind brings in a warm one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' signals the containment, giving HINOOK after the cold tap letter. The 'blow' of the surface seems to be wind, but it is a boxer's punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm dry wind blowing down the eastern slopes of the Rockies, so a warm wind.

clue.text: The Thunderer pinched by bald cow

indicators.note: being pinched by something means being squeezed inside it

parts.note: shorn means having had the hair or wool cut off, so bald
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Thor the god being nipped by a hairless cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thunderer' is also a nickname for The Times newspaper, but here it is the Norse god; 'pinched by' signals the squeeze into the word for bald.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of cattle with short horns, so an example of a cow.

clue.text: Stretch too far right with rugby players getting warmed up?

indicators.note: the oven is getting, or receiving, the pieces inside it

parts.note: things are warmed up in an oven
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Players warm up before a match that runs over time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'warmed up' is a playful pointer to where food is warmed; 'getting' signals it receives the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go beyond an allotted limit, extending past where one should stop.

clue.text: Difference in sequence

definitions.meaning: a disagreement or quarrel, as in a difference of opinion
a line of things one after another, as in three wins in succession

explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a difference between people; a line of things one after another forms a sequence.

clue.text: Novel finished about bovine going back into desert

indicators.note: the word for finished goes about, or around, the rest

parts.note: done means finished

indicators.note: the reversed animal goes into the word for desert

parts.note: to quit is to desert or abandon

indicators.note: going back means the letters are reversed

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A tale of a cow wandering back into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns OX into XO, which goes 'into' QUIT; DONE goes 'about' the lot. 'Novel' seems to be an adjective but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes' famous Spanish work, a classic example of a novel.

clue.text: Caribbean preserves about perfect

indicators.note: the two preserves are placed about, or around, the next piece

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
to can food is to preserve it
A1 means first-rate or perfect, here written AI

explanation.surface: Caribbean jams about which someone raves as perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserves' gives two words, JAM and CAN, placed 'about' AI. A1 (written AI) means perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Jamaica, an island country in the Caribbean, is an example of a Caribbean person.

clue.text: Public anger over heartless country destruction

indicators.note: destruction breaks up the remaining letters to rearrange them
the heart of the word is its middle letter, here removed

explanation.surface: People are furious about the ruin of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes out N, the middle letter of COUNTRY; 'destruction' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public protest of indignation; synonym for a storm of popular anger.

clue.text: Spots announcement of east end borough?

indicators.note: an announcement is something said out loud, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: Hackney is a borough in London's East End

explanation.surface: Asking for news of a borough in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough in the East End, where cockneys famously drop their H's: 'Ackney sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, which are commonly called spots.

clue.text: After cooking meats, I clear the restaurant

indicators.note: cooking the meat mixes it up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: net means clear after deductions, as in net profit

explanation.surface: A chef prepares meats, then I clear the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the meats into ESTAM. An estaminet is a small French café, a word British soldiers brought back from the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French café or bar serving food, so a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Nothing in drink on bar for Charlie, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another means it comes after it

parts.note: to check is to stop or bar

indicators.note: nothing is put inside the drink

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
O is the figure zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Ordering nothing to drink at the bar for a friend called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: Checkpoint Charlie was the famous Berlin Wall crossing point; 'Charlie' is also C in the NATO alphabet, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkpoint Charlie was the best-known crossing between East and West Berlin, an example of a border post.

clue.text: It may be great in name, but it's harmful in nature

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes inside the word for name

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

indicators.note: may be suggests the word great could be something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A thing that may be grand by reputation but is truly damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may be great' signals an anagram of GREAT (GARET), which goes 'in' CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke is a well-known health hazard, so it is damaging by nature.

clue.text: Loosely hang in tree — not hot in the shade

indicators.note: loosely suggests the letters are rearranged freely
not means the following letter is left out of the shuffled letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Something hangs limply in a tree, out of the heat in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange HANG IN TREE, leaving out H for hot. The shade sounds like shadow but is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-red colour named after the fruit, so a shade.

clue.text: Normal to keep silver fashionable

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: all there means mentally normal or sane
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Being conventional while holding on to silver is in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts AG inside ALL THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hugely popular at the moment is in vogue, an idiom for fashionable.

clue.text: Fast installing a very large number of sheds

indicators.note: installing means placing a piece inside

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A rapid installation of many garden sheds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installing' signals the containment; OS (outsize) is clothing-size shorthand for very large. 'Fast' seems to mean quickly but is the season of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean-tos are simple sheds built against a wall with a sloping roof.

clue.text: Nobleman given award in a flap

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A peer is all a-flutter on being given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flap' sounds like panic, but a flap is the definition. The OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft lobe hanging at the bottom of the ear is a flap of skin.

clue.text: Indian food which can be knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, and the word reads the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A snack you can wolf down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' sounds like eating or drinking quickly, but it means the word reversed, which is the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leavened flatbread from South Asia, an example of Indian food.

clue.text: Where in us summer afternoon's beginning

parts.note: August is a summer month

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Seeking a place in America at the start of a summer afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' disguises US, the United States. 'beginning' takes A from afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the United States, capital of Maine and also a city in Georgia, so a place there.

clue.text: Emperor waves, standing in anachronistic means of conveyance?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle, out of place in Roman times

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means the letters stand upright, read bottom to top

parts.note: the sea is the waves

explanation.surface: An emperor waves to the crowd while standing in a car, a vehicle out of its era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns SEA upwards to ESA, put 'in' CAR. The car is 'anachronistic' because Roman emperors had none.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used by Roman emperors after Julius, so a word for an emperor.

clue.text: More serene state, only brief

parts.note: Cal is the abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: mere means only, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: A government says it will be only briefly more peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the last E off MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning tranquil, so more peaceful.

clue.text: Regular shape with radius — vertical line inside irregular shape

indicators.note: the two letters are placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a tangle is a confused, irregular mass
the letter I looks like a vertical line

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson contrasting a neat figure with a messy one.
explanation.walkthrough: R and I go 'inside' TANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided figure, a familiar geometric shape; regular because its sides are straight.

clue.text: Nurse tackling it — one's painful affliction

parts.note: to tend is to nurse
on means engaged with or tackling, as in working on a problem
one is I, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A nurse dealing with a painful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', I + IS letters: I and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of a tendon, a painful condition of sinew and joint.

clue.text: Runner taking short jump

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to skip is to jump lightly

explanation.surface: An athlete doing a quick hop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts P off SKIP. 'Runner' looks like an athlete but is a runner on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is a long narrow blade on which something slides, as a ski does over snow.

clue.text: Fly east bypassing area, having doubled back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
doubled means the letters are written twice
bypassing means going round without including, so the letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A fly heads east, avoids a district and doubles back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bypassing' drops A from EAST, leaving EST; 'doubled' makes ESTEST; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An African bloodsucking insect that spreads sleeping sickness, an example of a fly.

clue.text: Smooth drop

definitions.meaning: to smooth is to remove creases, read playfully as the answer
a drop is a reduction or fall

explanation.definitionFit: To iron out wrinkles is to take creases out playfully; a fall in amount is a reduction.
